docs.title: Welcome to BRTA 2.0 Documentation
docs.text:
🚫 No Dalal, No Delay Smart Roads. Smart Drivers.Smart Traffic. Smart Bangladesh.

The future of transportation management in Bangladesh – fully digital, transparent, and citizen-centric.

docs.title: 🎯 Our Mission
docs.text: Transform Bangladesh's transportation services by leveraging cutting-edge digital technologies to eliminate corruption, reduce delays, and provide seamless access to essential BRTA services for every citizen.

docs.title: 🌟 Why BRTA 2.0?
docs.text:
⚡ No Middlemen

Say goodbye to illegal intermediaries (dalals). All services are 100% online and automated.

🚀 Instant Processing

Real-time verification, automated workflows, and immediate digital certificates.

🔒 Secure & Transparent

End-to-end encryption, digital audit trails, and complete transparency in every transaction.

docs.title: 🎓 Key Features Covered
docs.text:
• Driving License Management: Online applications, exam scheduling, digital licenses with QR codes
  • Vehicle Registration: Seamless registration and ownership transfer workflows
  • Route Permits: Multi-step approval system for transport operators
  • Payment Gateway: Secure online payments with SSLCommerz integration
  • AI Chatbot: 24/7 multilingual assistant powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite
  • Police Portal: Real-time verification and roadside enforcement tools
  • Admin Dashboard: Comprehensive management and analytics platform

docs.title: 💡 Project Vision🚦 Ready to Explore?
docs.text:
"To set a new standard for e-governance in Bangladesh's transportation sector, improving public satisfaction, operational efficiency, and eliminating systemic corruption."

BRTA 2.0 is not just a system – it's a movement towards a smarter, cleaner, and more accountable Bangladesh.

Start with Chapter 1: Introduction to understand the motivation behind BRTA 2.0, or jump directly to Chapter 2: Project Description to see how each module works.

docs.title: 1.1 Background
docs.text: Transportation services are a major component of national infrastructure. They are directly connected to public safety, mobility, and economic development. In Bangladesh, the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) is primarily responsible for issuing driving licenses, registering vehicles, managing route permits, and enforcing transportation regulations. With rapid population growth (about 173 million) and an increasing number of vehicles, the demand for efficient, reliable, and user-friendly transport-related services has risen significantly. Although digital initiatives have been introduced, many processes still involve manual verification, extensive physical paperwork, and in-person visits.

docs.title: 1.2 Purpose
docs.text:
The purpose of building the BRTA 2.0 system is to revolutionize the delivery of transportation-related services in Bangladesh by leveraging modern digital technologies. The system is designed to:

- Centralize all BRTA services (license issuance, vehicle registration, permit management, ownership transfer, etc.) into a single, integrated online platform.
  • Minimize manual intervention and physical paperwork, making processes faster, more reliable, and less prone to errors or corruption.
  • Enable real-time verification and validation of documents, reducing fraud and improving trust among citizens and authorities.
  • Enhance accessibility for all stakeholders, including citizens, administrators, and law enforcement, through a user-friendly, multilingual interface.
  • Foster transparency and accountability by providing clear digital records and audit trails for every transaction and interaction.
  • Support remote access and mobile-friendly features, allowing users to complete tasks from anywhere, at any time.

Ultimately, the BRTA 2.0 system aims to set a new standard for e-governance in Bangladesh’s transportation sector, improving public satisfaction and operational efficiency.

docs.title: 1.3 Objectives
docs.text:
The main objectives of the BRTA 2.0 system are:

  1. Process Automation: Digitize and automate the end-to-end workflows for driving license applications, vehicle registrations, route permits, ownership transfers, and renewals, reducing manual bottlenecks and paperwork.
  2. Real-Time Verification: Implement secure, instant verification of documents and credentials using QR codes, digital signatures, and integration with law enforcement databases.
  3. Integrated Payments: Provide seamless integration with payment gateways for online fee payments, ensuring secure, transparent, and traceable financial transactions.
  4. Stakeholder Coordination: Facilitate effective communication and coordination among citizens, BRTA staff, and police officers through role-based access and notification systems.
  5. Transparency and Accountability: Maintain comprehensive digital records and audit logs for all activities, making it easier to monitor, review, and resolve disputes or irregularities.
  6. User Experience: Deliver a modern, intuitive, and multilingual web portal that is accessible to users of all backgrounds, including support for mobile devices and assistive technologies.
  7. Fraud and Corruption Reduction: Minimize opportunities for illegal intermediaries (Dalals) and internal corruption by automating processes and increasing visibility into every transaction.
  8. Scalability and Future-Proofing: Design the system to be scalable and adaptable, allowing for future enhancements such as AI-powered chatbots, advanced analytics, and integration with other government services.

docs.title: 1.4 Problem in existing systems
docs.text: The existing BRTA service infrastructure suffers from fragmented workflows, limited automation, and a lack of real-time verification. Major issues include inefficient application processing, difficulty verifying driving licenses and vehicle documents, and limited technological support for enforcement authorities. In addition, the lack of seamless integration among users, administrators, and police officers restricts effective monitoring and governance.

docs.title: Benchmark: Existing System vs. BRTA 2.0 Solution
docs.text:
Problem Area Existing BRTA System BRTA 2.0 Solution Application Processing Manual, slow, requires physical visits Fully online, automated, fast Document Verification Manual, prone to errors and fraud Real-time, digital, QR code-based Payment Cash, in-person, risk of corruption Secure online payment gateway User Experience Complex, non-intuitive, language barriers Modern, user-friendly, multilingual Integration (Police/Admin) Poor, limited data sharing Seamless, real-time integration Transparency & Accountability Low, difficult to audit High, digital records and audit logs Notifications & Updates Manual, delayed, often missed Automated, instant, multi-channel Scalability Not scalable, bottlenecks with growth Designed for scalability and future enhancements Fraud & Intermediaries (Dalals) High risk, system inefficiencies exploited Reduced risk, automated workflows, transparency

Many studies on e-governance and public service digitization show the benefits of using digital platforms to improve efficiency and transparency in government services [1].

docs.title: 1.5 Motivation
docs.text: Although BRTA has an existing online portal, citizens still experience long delays, limited transparency, and complex procedures. Many people rely on computer operators at local shops to submit driving license applications. Applicants frequently need to visit BRTA offices multiple times for document submission, verification, and examinations. These challenges create opportunities for illegal intermediaries (known as dalals), who exploit system inefficiencies to demand extra money or bribes. As a result, public trust in the existing system has severely declined, and in some cases even internal officers and staff participate in these illegal practices. Therefore, a more reliable and transparent solution is urgently needed.

docs.title: Project Description
docs.text: The following chapter is the detailed description of the major functional modules of the BRTA 2.0 system. Each module is created to fulfill a particular need of the transport management ecosystem of Bangladesh to make it efficiently, transparently, and with user satisfaction.

docs.title: 2.1.1 User Authentication and Profile Management
docs.text:
Technical: Based on secure JWT-based authentication and Supabase as the back-end database. User registrations and logins use user credentials that are validated by registration and logins and assign roles (citizen, staff, police) where access is granted on a fine-grain level. Passwords have been hashed and stored in a secure location; OTP verification is done on password reset and other essential activities. RESTful APIs control user profiles, and role changes and updates are permitted.

User Interface: The users are allowed to sign up and also Log in with their mobile number or email address. The system takes them through OTP authentication to enhance security. The profile management process is also user-friendly, wherein an individual is able to change personal details and passwords. There are dedicated dashboards with additional controls on staff and police.

docs.title: 2.1.2 Driving License Management
docs.text:
Technical: License application forms contain dynamic validation and support document uploading (PDF/JPG). The calendar API is applied in exam scheduling, which takes physical and online exam slots. Supabase tables hold the license information, and workflow provides statuses. A (server-side) library helps create digital licenses with unique QR codes which are instantly verifiable by scanning.

User Experience: The applicants complete a online form, submit documents and choose dates of exams. They are notified regarding applications and test schedule. Past generation- After completion, we can download a digital license, which is instantaneous to verify by the authorities through the QR code. Checking is done automatically through scripts which compare the data submitted and the government records. Status events result in notification events through email/SMS APIs.

docs.title: 2.1.3 Vehicle Registration and Ownership Transfer
docs.text:
Technical: These workflows are based on form and document uploading in vehicle registration and ownership transfer modules. Verification automatic Backend scripts are used to compare submitted data against government records. The changes in status cause notification events through email/SMS APIs.

User Experience: The user has an option of registering new cars or transferring ownership of the vehicles online by filling in forms and uploading documents. The system reminds them about renewals and checks up on them. Everything is available in the user dashboard.

docs.title: 2.1.4 Route Permit Management
docs.text:
Technical: Route permit applications are handled using a multi-step approval workflow, which is operated by Supabase triggers and role-based access. This is then integrated with the police systems through secure REST APIs, and permit validation can be done in real time. Renewal, cancellation is done through updating of permit records and reporting to the concerned parties.

User Experience: The transport operators request route permits online, monitor approvals and/or get notifications. BRTA and police employees countercheck permits online and minimize the time spent on paperwork and delays. Renewals and cancellations can be done with a couple of clicks.

docs.title: 2.1.5 Payment Gateway Integration
docs.text:
Technical: Payments can be done via third-party gateways (SSLCommerz) which have been integrated through secure API end-points. Every single transaction is recorded in Supabase, and electronic receipts are created and sent to the users via email. Service workflows are connected with payment status; in this manner only paid applications could be provided.

User Experience: The client can make payments safely and online using their favorite mode of payment. The system has immediate confirmation and online receipts. The user dashboard contains payment history.

docs.title: 2.1.6 Chatbot Assistance
docs.text:
Technical: The chatbot service in the backend is provided by Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite to achieve quick and affordable AI responses. Handling of session management is done in memory with automatically cleaned up inactive sessions. The chatbot is strict in terms of topic (BRTA-related queries only). Multi-language assistive is added by transmitting the user language preferences to the AI API.

User Experiences: It has a chatbot where the users can get real-time assistance and instructions in English and Bangali. Off topic questions To maintain a focus on the conversation, off topic questions are gracefully rejected.

docs.title: 2.1.7 Admin Dashboard
docs.text:
Technical: Built with current frontend frameworks (React) and integrated Supabase to update data in real time. It displays application statistics, approval queues and health metrics of the system and analytics charts and downloadable reports. Only authorized staff will be able to access role management and audit logs.

User Experience: BRTA employees can review applications, grant requests and check the systems health on a single dashboard.

docs.title: 2.1.8 Police Portal
docs.text:
Technical: Police officers are subjected to a secure portal allowing them to access secured information based on authentication and other role-centric rules. The process of verification in real-time is made possible through QRane scanning and Supabase record querying. The portal has overlaying search and filtering capabilities to rapidly access vehicle and license information.

User Experience: These will allow the police to check licenses, vehicle registrations, and route permits by scan or search of records. The portal is used to simplify roadside checking and enforcement, and minimize paperwork and delays in the manual system.

docs.title: 2.1.9 Notification
docs.text:
Technical: Messages are dispatched through high-level email and SMS APIs. Application notification System Backend event triggers and frontend state handling in-app notifications. Form based user feedback is stored and used by the support staff, ticket management is used via Supabase tables.

User Experience: It is done through email, texts, and in-app notifications that inform users of the status of an application, timetables, and renewals. They are able to provide feedback or support requests, which are monitored and addressed by the staff through industry standard methods of encryption at rest. Authentication Intermediate and Input Checking Secure the API Endpoints. The system would be in line with the data protection laws in Bangladesh and the system gets subjected to frequent security audits. Ongoing maintenance includes the vulnerability scanning and management of a patch.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text: This chapter outlines the technologies, frameworks, and tools used to build the BRTA 2.0 system. The chosen tech stack ensures scalability, security, and a seamless user experience for all stakeholders.

docs.title: 3.1 Frontend
docs.text:
• Framework: React.js for building dynamic, responsive user interfaces.
  • UI Library: Tailwind CSS for consistent and modern design.
  • Routing: React Router DOM for client-side navigation.
  • Animation: Framer Motion and Lottie for interactive UI elements.
  • Charting: Recharts for analytics and reporting dashboards.

docs.title: 3.2 Backend
docs.text:
• Runtime: Node.js for scalable server-side logic.
  • Framework: Express.js for RESTful API development.
  • Database: Supabase (PostgreSQL) for secure, scalable data storage and real-time updates.
  • File Storage: Supabase Storage for document uploads and digital license storage.

docs.title: 3.3 AI & Chatbot
docs.text:
• AI Service: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite for fast, cost-effective chatbot responses.
  • Session Management: In-memory storage (Map) for active chat sessions.
  • Language Support: API integration for English and Bangla responses.

docs.title: 3.4 Payment Integration
docs.text: • Gateway: SSLCommerz for secure online payments.

docs.title: 3.5 Notifications
docs.text:
• Email: Nodemailer for transactional and notification emails.
  • In-app: Custom notification system using frontend state and backend event triggers.

docs.title: 3.6 Security
docs.text:
• Encryption: TLS/SSL for data in transit, AES for data at rest.
  • Validation: Input validation and sanitization at both frontend and backend.
  • Compliance: Adherence to Bangladesh’s data protection laws and regular security audits.

docs.title: 3.7 Deployment
docs.text: • Hosting: Vercel or custom VPS for frontend; Supabase and Node.js server for backend.

docs.title: Authentication and Security
docs.text: In this chapter, the author describes the authentication processes and security practices that are adopted to enforce user data, user privacy, and system integrity in the BRTA 2.0 system.

docs.title: 4.1 Authentication
docs.text:
User Registration / Login: Users (citizens, staff, police) can register and log in through the use of their mobile number or email address. Authored credentials are checked against records that are stored in Supabase.

Password Management: Hashing of passwords is done before storage. The password change is done through the OTP verification that is sent to the registered contact.

Session Management: Secure tokens are used in managing authenticated sessions. Auto-cleanup processes and session time outs serve to eliminate unauthorized access.

Role-Based Access Control: Every user receives a role (citizen, staff, police) according to which he/she has a specific access level and access features. Frontend and backend role checks are implemented.

docs.title: 4.2 Security Practices
docs.text:
Data Encryption: Sensitive data is transmitted and stored encrypted with TLS/SSL and encrypted with AES, respectively.

Security of API: API endpoints are secured with Authentication middleware, input validation and CORS policy to minimize cross-site attacks and illegal access.

Environment Variables: Environment variables contain secrets called API keys, database credentials among others and are never coded.

Input Verification and Sanitizing: The frontend and the backend sanitizing and verifying the inputs minimize risks likes the SQL injection and XSS.

Audit Logging: The action and changes which are the most critical are logged to be monitored and analyzed.

Conformance to laws: The system complies with data protection laws in Bangladesh, and it is reviewed on a regular basis to ascertain its security levels.

Automated Cleanup: In-memory session data and expired tokens are periodically deleted in order to reduce the risk and to enhance the performance.

docs.title: 4.3 User Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Privacy Policy: Users are educated by a transparent privacy policy about the information they gathered, their usage and our protection of it.

User Control: The user is capable of passing information about themselves, as well as altering passwords safely via their own profile dashboard.

Security Event Notification: Notices are supplied to users about security-related events, e.g. password alterations or dubious log-in.

docs.title: Version Control and Collaboration
docs.text: This chapter describes the version control system and collaboration practices used by the BRTA 2.0 development team to ensure code quality, traceability, and efficient teamwork.

docs.title: 5.1 Version Control System
docs.text:
• System Used: Git is used for distributed version control, with all code hosted on GitHub.
  • Repositories: The project consists of a main code repository and a separate design repository, both linked for seamless development and UI/UX integration.
  • Branching Strategy:
  • main branch for ongoing development and integration.
  • deployment-ready branch for stable releases and production deployment.
  • Feature and bugfix branches are created for individual tasks and merged after review.
  • Commit Practices:
  • Team members commit changes regularly with clear, descriptive messages.
  • Pull requests are used for merging, with mandatory code reviews to maintain quality.
  • Merge conflicts are resolved collaboratively, ensuring no loss of work.
  • Tagging & Releases:
  • Major releases are tagged for easy rollback and deployment tracking.

docs.title: 5.2 Collaboration Insights
docs.text:
• Team Structure: Five developers contributed to the project, dividing tasks based on expertise (frontend, backend, design, integration).
  • Design Repository: The design repository contains UI/UX assets and prototypes, kept in sync with the main codebase for consistent user experience.
  • Task Assignment: Tasks are assigned and tracked using GitHub Issues and Discussions, with regular standups for progress updates.
  • Code Review: Every pull request is reviewed by at least one other team member before merging, ensuring code quality and knowledge sharing.
  • Continuous Integration: Automated checks run on each pull request to catch errors early and maintain stability.
  • Benefits:
  • Enables traceability of changes and accountability.
  • Facilitates teamwork and parallel development.
  • Provides a clear audit trail and rollback capability.
  • Streamlines deployment and release management.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: In this chapter, the author outlines the two primary categories of automated tests which are employed in BRTA 2.0 system in order to guarantee reliability, accuracy, and quality user experience.

docs.title: 6.1 API Testing
docs.text: Framework: Python, pytest Intention: Checks the health of backend API along with endpoint availability, response header and the configuration of CORS. Process: Tests are secure and are not elemental (do not update data). Pytest is used to test and produce Excel and HTML reports. Examples of these tests are server availability, response time, checking of header and CORS verification. Reporting: Visual results, condition, and time are recorded when a specific test is run.

docs.title: 6.2 Selenium UI Testing
docs.text: Framework: Python, pytest, Selenium WebDriver. Purpose: Tools Browser-based user flows are automatable To be tested On the end-to-end testing. Process: Includes authentication, licencing application, payment, booking, and so on. Processes user actions (was clicks and form fills) and verifies responses of the UI. Captures screen shots and records the results of every test step. Produces test result Excel reports. Example Scenarios: Login and signup flow, Password reset, Applications and renewal of license, Licensing and payment of digital license, Reserving and scheduling physical examination appointments.

docs.title: 6.3 Test Coverage and Quality
docs.text: Coverage: Both API and UI tests are concerned with essential modules (authentication, payments, chatbot, booking and so on). Continuous Testing: Automated tests are executing at the regular periods and at every monumental update, to identify the regressions at an early stage. Bug Tracking: During the testing process, the issues are reported in GitHub Issues and addressed before launch.

docs.title: Future Work
docs.text: This chapter summarizes the improvements and directions that the BRTA 2.0 system will undertake to enhance impact, scalability, and user experience.

docs.title: 7.1 Mobile Application
docs.text: Create dedicated Android and iOS applications to enable users to access BRTA services, notifications, and electronic documents on the go. The mobile app can also support push notifications, biometric login, and offline access to essential documents.

docs.title: 7.2 NID Database Integration
docs.text: Integrate with the National ID (NID) database to verify user identity instantly and securely during registration and application submission. This will help prevent fraud and reduce manual verification steps.

docs.title: 7.3 Scalability Enhancements
docs.text: Horizontally scale the backend architecture to support increasing user load and transaction volume. Load balancing, caching, and database optimization can improve availability and performance.

docs.title: 7.4 LLM-Based Chatbot
docs.text: Develop an advanced chatbot based on Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on BRTA-specific data. This will enable more natural, context-sensitive, and multilingual support for BRTA services and user needs. The chatbot can handle complex requests, provide personalized assistance, and integrate with all BRTA 2.0 modules.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The BRTA 2.0 program is a major step toward the digitalization of transportation services in Bangladesh. The platform addresses long-standing challenges in efficiency, transparency, and accessibility by using modern technologies, robust security practices, and a user-centric design. The modular structure of the system, integrated authentication, and streamlined processes enable citizens, administrators, and law enforcement to access BRTA services conveniently and securely.

With extensive testing, collaborative development practices, and planned enhancements such as a mobile application, NID database integration, scalability improvements, and an advanced chatbot, BRTA 2.0 can evolve to meet changing demands and technological progress. The project not only modernizes current operational procedures but also lays the foundation for a clearer, more accountable, and more user-friendly public service ecosystem.

Overall, BRTA 2.0 is an example of innovation, collaboration, and public trust aligned with Bangladesh’s digital governance initiatives. Continued maintenance and responsiveness to user feedback will help ensure that the system remains relevant, resilient, and impactful in the future.
